description: cargo build --release --lib currently emits 273 warnings from crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/ (86 unused fns, 60 unused consts, 51 unused imports, 28 never-constructed structs, plus smaller unused-trait/enum/type-alias/assoc-item clusters). Per this crate's CLAUDE.md these are reference OpenFOAM solver ports (rhoPimpleFoam, driftFluxFoam, etc.) intended for future transient two-phase coupling -- so this is NOT a blind delete-everything pass. Before removing anything: for each warning, decide (a) genuinely dead and safe to delete, or (b) kept intentionally for a not-yet-wired future consumer, in which case wire the consumer or add a scoped #[allow(dead_code)] with a comment explaining why, rather than silently deleting planned scaffolding. cargo fix --lib -p tampines-steam-tables --allow-dirty can auto-resolve the unused-import subset (~48 suggestions per the build output) as a safe first pass. User request 2026-07-13: 'eventually' cleanup, not urgent -- P4.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
2026-07-13: Silenced (not deleted) for now, per user request -- don't want lints eating context budget while other work is in flight. Added #[allow(dead_code, unused_imports)] to each `pub(crate) mod X;` / `pub(crate) use X::*;` declaration in openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/mod.rs (cascades to the whole submodule tree -- verified this via a throwaway test crate before applying). cargo build --release --lib -p tampines-steam-tables is now 0 warnings.
Still tracked here as future work: revisit each ported primitive and decide delete vs. wire up a real consumer vs. keep the #[allow] with a stated reason -- the suppression is a stopgap, not a resolution. Also note this directory has its own CLAUDE.md (openfoam_algorithms/CLAUDE.md) documenting a WIP HEM rhoPimpleFoam solver (TampinesSteamArray, already merged to develop) and a feature/validation branch policy for that specific task -- unrelated to this lint-suppression edit, but worth reading before doing substantive work in this directory.

title: Clean up 273 dead-code/unused-import warnings in openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source

description:
Found incidentally while doing op-uyi3 (2026-08-13). Not caused by that work and not fixed by it -- that session's file ownership was limited to steam_turbine_equations/.

crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/interfaces/functional_programming/pt_flash_eqm/multiphase_flashing.rs:176-177 has two UNCONDITIONAL dbg! calls on a production code path:

    dbg!(&near_critical_point);
    dbg!(&(near_saturation_line, h_liq, h_vap, h_saturated));

They fire from h_tp_eqm_two_phase whenever the Region 3 two-phase branch is taken, i.e. for any near-critical saturated-state property call, in release builds as well as debug. dbg! writes to stderr and is not gated by any feature or cfg.

Reproduction (observed): calling h_tp_eqm_two_phase(sat_temp_4(p0), p0, 0.0) and (.., 1.0) at p0 = 20 MPa emits four multi-line dbg! blocks to stderr, e.g.

  [.../multiphase_flashing.rs:176:13] &near_critical_point = false
  [.../multiphase_flashing.rs:177:13] &(near_saturation_line, h_liq, h_vap, h_saturated) = (
      true,
      1827100.5374104856 m^2 s^-2,
      ...

Note the line immediately above them is a dbg! that was already commented out, which suggests these two were meant to go the same way and were missed.

Impact: stderr noise in any consumer that touches near-critical saturation properties (the FHR simulator examples, TampinesSteamArray, any transient near the critical point), plus a real per-call formatting cost on a hot property path. It also pollutes test output, which is how it was noticed.

Fix: delete both lines, or gate them behind a feature/cfg(debug_assertions) if they are still wanted for diagnosis. Worth grepping the crate for other unconditional dbg!/println! on property paths at the same time -- choked_flow/mod.rs's get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_with_stagnation_props already carries a hard-coded debug=true flag that its own doc comment flags as a WIP artefact.
title: tampines-steam-tables: unconditional dbg! in production path h_tp_eqm_two_phase (Region 3)

description: The graph digitiser (bead op-5v5.8) shipped with three binaries: kovan-digitise (CLI), kovan-digitise-tui (ratatui), kovan-digitise-gui (egui, non-default digitise-gui feature). The engine and CLI are covered by synthetic self-consistency tests and a scripted end-to-end run; the TUI and GUI compile (desktop + aarch64-linux-android check for the TUI, desktop for the GUI) and the TUI --help path was exercised, but NEITHER HYBRID FRONT END HAS BEEN DRIVEN INTERACTIVELY - the implementing session had no TTY or display. A human needs to: run kovan-digitise-tui auto over a real image and check overlay/nudge/delete/review/save; run kovan-digitise-gui (cargo run --release -p kovan-literature --bin kovan-digitise-gui --features digitise-gui), place refs, auto-trace, drag/add/delete, mark reviewed + save; confirm the saved JSON records HandCorrected/HandPlaced origins and the Reviewed{by,at,interface} stamp. Until then treat both hybrid front ends as untested-interactively AI draft.
title: kovan-literature digitiser: maintainer hand-test of the TUI and egui review front ends

description: There is NO criterion dependency and NO benches/ directory anywhere in the workspace; the single in-repo microbenchmark is a hand-rolled Instant::now() pair inside a unit test (teh-o-prke/src/delayed_neutron_layer.rs:554). Every performance claim in the repository except the CIET figure and the delayed-neutron layer is prose asserted by nothing, so regressions are invisible. Land this early enough that the chem-eng O(1) rewrite and the TUAS Thomas-solver swap can be SHOWN to have worked rather than asserted. Note the recent chem-eng measurement (28 us/step plateau) was taken with a throwaway example that had to be deleted -- that is the gap this closes.
title: workspace: add a criterion bench harness and one committed baseline per band

description: Four mandatory benchmarks: (1) infinite homogeneous medium vs analytical k_inf; (2) U235 sphere vs OpenMC; (3) TRISO in graphite, RSA vs CLS vs SCLS; (4) B4C burnable-poison particles, RSA vs CLS vs SCLS. Per workspace V&V rule the docs must record BOTH methodology and measured results with uncertainty + date/data-version — no result may be quoted until the run actually happens. Per the crate rule, OpenMC reference values come from the openmc .ipynb cell outputs, and comparison CSVs go to the gitignored verification_and_validation/openmc_notebook_comparisons/.
title: outram-mc: stochastic-media benchmark suite RSA vs CLS vs SCLS (design doc s18)

title: outram-blender: modifier stack (subsurf/mirror/array)

description:
crates/teh-o-prke/src/decay_heat.rs:12 carries the original author own comment doubting its correctness on unit grounds. It is also not currently wired into htgr_sim_v1 at all.

SCOPE: verify the existing implementation against a standard decay-heat curve, fix or replace it, and wire it into the simulator. An ANS-5.1-form decay-heat standard curve with open published coefficients is the natural reference.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE: the entire passive safety case is a decay-heat removal argument. A loss-of-forced-cooling transient computed with a wrong decay-heat source is meaningless no matter how good the conduction model is.

Record the verification numbers and the reference curve in the test doc comment per the V&V rule. Related: op-7rf covers a decay-heat sign error in the melcor work — check whether the same error class is present here.
title: HTR-10: fix or replace decay heat — currently self-flagged as suspect
